security_audit.summary: The two static network findings are repository links in SKILL.md, not executable requests or exfiltration paths. No prompt injection, code execution, credential access, or unsafe instructions were found in the reviewed prompt-only skill.

finding_verdicts.reason: The URL is metadata pointing to the upstream source repository. It does not trigger a network request or instruct data transmission.
The URL is a documentation link for more information. The prompt-only skill contains no code that connects to that URL.

content.value_statement: Web testers need focused ffuf guidance when planning directory, parameter, or virtual host fuzzing. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a simple workflow for web fuzzing discussions.
actual_capabilities: Provides a concise purpose statement for ffuf-based web fuzzing.
Frames when to use the skill for authorized web fuzzing tasks.
Guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward ffuf workflow discussions.
References the upstream source repository for additional context.
Operates as guidance only and does not include executable automation.
limitations: It does not include detailed ffuf command recipes in the current file.
It does not verify target ownership or legal authorization.
It does not run scans, parse results, or manage wordlists.
It depends on the assistant to apply safe testing practices.

use_cases.title: Plan Authorized Discovery
use_cases.description: Create a focused ffuf testing plan for an approved web application scope.

use_cases.title: Support Training Labs
use_cases.description: Explain where ffuf fits in controlled web security exercises.

use_cases.title: Prepare Review Notes
use_cases.description: Summarize planned fuzzing scope, expected signals, and review checkpoints before testing starts.

prompt_templates.title: Explain ffuf Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what ffuf is, when to use it, and what authorization checks I need before testing.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an authorized ffuf web fuzzing session for this staging application scope: [scope].

prompt_templates.title: Improve Signal Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my authorized ffuf test goals and suggest response filters, rate limits, and result triage steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Team Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized ffuf workflow for a security team, including scope control, evidence handling, and reporting handoff.

output_examples.input: I need a safe plan for ffuf content discovery on my staging site.
output: Confirms authorization and scope before testing.
Lists target areas, wordlist selection criteria, filters, and rate limits.
Adds review steps for false positives and reporting.

output_examples.input: My ffuf results include many repeated responses.
output: Suggests comparing response size, status, redirect behavior, and word count.
Recommends documenting assumptions before excluding responses.
Keeps manual validation before any conclusion.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization and scope before planning any fuzzing activity.
Use rate limits and filters that match the target environment.
Review findings manually before reporting security impact.
anti_patterns: Do not fuzz systems without explicit permission.
Do not launch high-volume scans against fragile or shared services.
Do not treat status codes as proof without content validation.

faq.question: What is ffuf?
faq.answer: ffuf is a fast web fuzzing tool used for authorized content and parameter discovery.

faq.question: Does this skill run ffuf?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance for assistant conversations and does not execute scans.

faq.question: Can I use it on public sites?
faq.answer: Use it only when you have explicit permission and a defined scope.

faq.question: Does it include wordlists?
faq.answer: No. The current skill file does not include wordlists or bundled assets.

faq.question: Which tools support it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What safety checks should I apply?
faq.answer: Confirm authorization, limit request volume, and validate findings manually.
